newsitem.title: INDIA: India targets fraud at state banks - Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: India targets fraud at state banks - Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Tuesday the government was taking steps to improve the profitability of state-owned banks and constantly reviewing their performance to reduce fraud.
Chidambaram said in a written statement presented to the upper house of parliament that the government was also taking measures to reduce fraud and irregularities in the banking system.

He said that in 1995/96 (April-March), "the overall position of banks was reviewed critically by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and specific directions to improve workings of the banks with broad emphasis on upgradation/recovery of non-performing assets...income/ profitability were issued".
There are 27 state-owned state-owned banks in India.
In 1995/96, eight public sector banks incurred a net loss of 25.90 billion rupees, the statement said.
The banks were Indian Bank, Vijaya Bank, UCO Bank, United Bank of India, State Bank of Saurashtra, Punjab and Sindh Bank, Punjab National Bank and Central Bank of India.

Chidambaram said the main reasons for losses suffered by these banks were provisioning for non-performing assets, provision for depreciation in government securities and payouts on account of wage revisions.
The finance minister said that in 1995 and up to March 1996, 38 employees of public sector banks were convicted and 1,467 employees were given penalties, including the dismissal of 379 for fraud.

"Thus it may be seen that the performance of public sector banks is reviewed on a continuing basis and all possible measures to improve their profitability and to minimise the incidence of occurrence of frauds/irregularities are taken from time to time," he said.
